# Crypto wallet interaction for bots on Base

# Crypto wallet interaction for bots on Base — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Crypto wallet interaction for bots on Base. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-06 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Structure and components

- [statement] Base documents the GasPriceOracle getL1Fee method for a serialized transaction and getL1FeeUpperBound for an approximate byte length. These provide transaction-size-sensitive estimates of the L1 component. (low confidence) — https://docs.base.org/specifications/transactions/network-fees

## How it works

- [statement] Base documents ETH as the currency of its Mainnet and lists separate public RPC and transaction-submission endpoints for Mainnet and Sepolia. It says to use the transaction submission endpoint only to send transactions and the RPC endpoint for all other requests; use these network settings when configuring an Ethereum wallet library for Base. (low confidence) — https://docs.base.org/base-chain/quickstart/connecting-to-base
- [statement] Viem createNonceManager automatically generates transaction nonces for Local Accounts. The documentation assigns nonce management for JSON-RPC Accounts to their wallet or backend; it does not describe this manager as a cross-process coordinator. (low confidence) — https://viem.sh/docs/accounts/local/createNonceManager
- [statement] Base fee budgeting must account for L1 publication cost as well as L2 execution. Its detailed fee formula also includes operatorFee; the documentation says getOperatorFee returns zero when operator-fee parameters are zero. Do not treat gasUsed times effectiveGasPrice alone as the full fee. (low confidence) — https://docs.base.org/specifications/transactions/network-fees
- [statement] Safe implements ERC-4337 compatibility through Safe4337Module and a fallback handler. Its documented flow validates owner signatures on a UserOperation and executes it through EntryPoint; this flow does not itself establish a separate bot session-key permission policy. (low confidence) — https://docs.safe.global/advanced/erc-4337/4337-safe
- [statement] EIP-7702 sets persistent EOA code delegation. A processed delegation is not rolled back when transaction execution fails; the viem guide likewise shows subsequent calls without a new authorization. (medium confidence) — https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7702 · keywords: Crypto wallet interaction for bots on Base · also: https://viem.sh/docs/eip7702/sending-transactions
- [statement] Viem documents executor: self for signAuthorization when the authorizing EOA also executes the transaction, because authorization.nonce must be one greater than transaction.nonce. The EIP processes authorization tuples after incrementing the sender nonce. (medium confidence) — https://viem.sh/docs/eip7702/sending-transactions · keywords: Crypto wallet interaction for bots on Base · also: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7702

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] ERC-7715 defines wallet_requestExecutionPermissions with a chainId, session account in to, permission and optional rules; the returned response may differ from the request. Discover supported permission and rule types rather than assuming every wallet accepts the same policy. (low confidence) — https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7715
- [statement] ERC-7715 defines permission revocation and retrieval methods and says unsupported wallets should return an error. Its interface specifies wallet-to-DApp interaction rather than how the wallet enforces permissions. (low confidence) — https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7715

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Viem Local Accounts keep signing keys on the consuming machine and sign before JSON-RPC broadcast. Its documented setup creates a Wallet Client and constructs a local account with privateKeyToAccount. (low confidence) — https://viem.sh/docs/accounts/local
- [statement] The viem local-account example extends a Wallet Client with publicActions and calls a contract simulation public action before a contract write wallet action; these are separate public simulation and wallet write actions. (low confidence) — https://viem.sh/docs/accounts/local
- [statement] web3.py documents explicit offline signing with sign_transaction followed by send_raw_transaction, or automatic signing through SignAndSendRawMiddlewareBuilder. Its guide says never to commit the private key in code. (low confidence) — https://web3py.readthedocs.io/en/stable/transactions.html
- [statement] The web3.py explicit transaction example obtains nonce from get_transaction_count and sets gas, maxFeePerGas, and maxPriorityFeePerGas before signing; contract calls can use build_transaction before the same signing and submission stages. (low confidence) — https://web3py.readthedocs.io/en/stable/transactions.html
- [statement] Safe Modules can automate DeFi actions without manual approvals, but enabled modules validate requests using their own rules and can execute arbitrary transactions. Safe explicitly warns that a malicious module can take over a Safe. (low confidence) — https://docs.safe.global/advanced/smart-account-modules
- [statement] EIP-7702 enables weaker sub-key permissions as a design goal, but secure delegate code must enforce replay protection and bind value, gas, target and calldata. ERC-7715 separately says wallet implementations must correctly enforce granted permissions and recommends limited scope and reasonable expiry. (medium confidence) — https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7702 · keywords: Crypto wallet interaction for bots on Base · also: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7715
- [statement] The cached ERC-7715 source is marked Draft. Treat the described method names as a proposal interface and verify the selected wallet implementation before depending on it. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7715
